items.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006
items.q: There was a guy named George Rudder who had a piano player... He had a band called the Oriskany Rhythm Kings

ctx.x: Was the band an entity at Hamilton as well? It sounds like you went off campus to play a lot of your gigs.

Yes. Good question, and I think in two ways. Number one, Hamilton was very small then, you know six, seven hundred students. Very isolated. The interstate had just opened, I mean so things were very much clustered around here. So everybody knew what was going on. And if we all got snowed in here we’d have a jam session. There were some other musicians here. There was a guy named George Rudder who had a piano player who is actually a very good piano player who plays out in the midwest. He had a band called the…

than the Catatonic Five. But anyway, so we’d get together and play. We’d play for house parties here obviously. Occasionally they’d hire us as a jam session here and so everybody knew the band and it was kind of a — music in those days, live music, was a focal point of parties. I mean you’d get a band and then you’d have a party, which was sort of neat. And so you needed to have the band to have the party. So in that sense we really were a part of the college.
